original_test_intent: Verify complete OS-visible hardware matches actual BIOS/platform configuration and remains stable across the approved time synchronization and three reboot cycles.
original_method: Agent collects complete raw inventory and comparisons; operator approves/supervises time change and each reboot through KVM/OOB with health/log evidence after every cycle.
manual_activity: User approves hardware map, time policy and critical reboot window; operator supervises NTP and three tracked reboot cycles with KVM/OOB recovery.
required_inputs: Approved NTP source/authentication and time-change policy
Decision whether reboot -f is mandatory plus three-cycle timing/health gates
Maintenance window, workload quiescence, backup, KVM/OOB and known-event policy
safety_requirements: Do not change time or reboot before explicit phase approval
Quiesce workloads and verify filesystem/RAID/boot/thermal health before every cycle
Use complete output and supported sysfs/USB interfaces rather than obsolete-path absence
Stop on mismatch, time/auth issue, unclean boot, storage/USB/PCI/BMC fault, hang or recovery loss
Do not force additional cycles or erase baseline logs
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete CPU/memory/DMI/PCI/storage/SCSI/USB inventory and compare to map
Capture NTP before/after audit if approved
Track each reboot timestamp, boot identity, enumeration and health/log delta
Do not approve force reboot, repair storage, change hardware/time independently or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve hardware map, NTP and force-reboot policy
Review inventory and every cycle to decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: lscpu/lsmem/lsblk/lspci cover only part of the source; head truncation and omission of DMI/SCSI/USB/time/reboots cause coverage regression.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Collect complete raw procfs, dmidecode, lspci, lsblk/fdisk, sg_map, lsusb/sysfs and BMC evidence; separately gate NTP and each tracked reboot through KVM/OOB.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NTP-first sequence, all listed hardware domains, three manual reboot -f cycles, Criteria and source 5/5 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a stable identity/topology matrix before state changes, then compare it and health/log deltas after each individually supervised reboot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces interactive vi and truncated snippets with complete raw evidence while retaining time and reboot coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Inventory is automated; time/reboot actions remain user-confirmed and operator-supervised.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Force reboot can corrupt active filesystems and NTP steps can disrupt timestamp continuity.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must decide whether reboot -f is truly required versus orderly reboot and define supported USB inventory path plus NTP/log-correlation policy; the agent cannot weaken or reinterpret those steps.
expected_evidence: NTP source plus before/after time and log audit
Per-cycle KVM/OOB reboot timestamps, boot IDs and enumeration comparisons
Mismatch/known-event triage, final stable state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require broad hardware comparison and reboot stability; obsolete USB-path wording is a platform applicability issue, not a competing source intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Hardware map, tools, time policy, reboot window and recovery are supplyable inputs; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Restores omitted DMI/SCSI/USB/time/reboot coverage and separates low-risk inventory from critical state-changing phases with per-cycle recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A pre-reboot inventory can appear correct even when firmware enumeration is unstable across boots, while truncated output can hide missing devices. Stable IDs and complete topology must be compared after each boot ID; because NTP changes timestamps and reboot -f can bypass orderly shutdown, the time audit and filesystem/RAID health are essential to interpret logs safely.
